evidence: Figure 7.4 caption: "Totals exclude padding, headers, extra copies, the separate per-tensor FP32 scale, and high-precision exceptions — so the bar totals omit the 4 B global scale that §7.3.3's worked example adds back (16,777,216 × 0.5625 + 4 = 9,437,188 B)."
issue: The arithmetic in the caption is correct (16,777,216 × 0.5625 = 9,437,184; +4 = 9,437,188), but the figure's NVFP4 bar is drawn at 18 B per 32 values, which represents 16 payload + 2 local-scale bytes. The caption says the bar totals 'omit the 4 B global scale' — true — but it does not clarify that the 18 B bar also omits the per-tensor FP32 global scale that §7.3.3's worked example explicitly adds. A reader comparing the figure's bar width to the worked-example byte count will see a 4-byte discrepancy with no visual cue. The caption text and figure bar widths are consistent with each other, but the figure's visual proportion (18/17 ≈ 1.06× MXFP4) does not visually encode the global-scale overhead at all, while the worked example's 9,437,188 B does. This is a minor presentation inconsistency, not an arithmetic error.
fix_instruction: Either add a note in the figure that the bar widths are local-scale-only and the global FP32 scale is not shown, or annotate the NVFP4 bar with '+4 B global' to make the visual and the worked-example total reconcile without a caption lookup.

evidence: Table 5-2, row 'Total tokens per dollar (serial single-stream floor, no overlap; 20 ms/token basis)': "~242,000 tokens per dollar (~199,000 at the canonical 25 ms/token)" with derivation "9,500/7.08 ≈ 1,342 tok/s × 3600 ÷ $20; 7.08 s = 1.08 s prefill + 6.0 s decode at the illustrative 20 ms/token rate; at the canonical 25 ms/token, 9,500/8.58 ≈ 1,107 tok/s ≈ 199,000 tokens/$"

fix_instruction: Split the row into two rows or move the ~199,000 figure to a separate footnote line, so each row carries exactly one basis and one provenance tag.

evidence: "single‑core encoding fits only above ≈92.8 GFLOP/s sustained per core (11.14 GFLOP ÷ 0.12 s), beyond that typical sustained range — conditional on measured single-core throughput."
issue: The sentence is grammatically broken: 'fits only above ≈92.8 GFLOP/s ... beyond that typical sustained range' reads as if 92.8 is beyond the range, but the intended meaning is that the required 92.8 GFLOP/s is beyond the 30–60 GFLOP/s typical sustained range, so single-core encoding does NOT fit. The clause 'beyond that typical sustained range' has no clear antecedent and the sentence lacks a main verb connecting the two halves. This is a prose clarity defect (ASD-STE100) that could mislead a reader into thinking single-core encoding fits.
fix_instruction: Rewrite as: 'single-core encoding would require ≈92.8 GFLOP/s sustained per core (11.14 GFLOP ÷ 0.12 s), which is beyond the typical 30–60 GFLOP/s sustained range — so single-core encoding does not fit the ~120 ms retrieval budget, conditional on measured single-core throughput.'

evidence: "The ~655K input-tokens-per-$1 alternative divides the $87,600 paid-for-730-h month by the same month's ~57.4B input tokens (6.24M requests × 9,200 = 57.4B) — an active-hours (173.33 h) volume, not a 730-hour volume. The 730-hour volume at the same 92,000 tok/s offered rate would be ~241.8B (92,000 × 3,600 × 730), so the two tokens-per-dollar figures differ only in the hour count in the denominator (173.33 vs 730), not in the workload or the fleet"
issue: The arithmetic is correct (6.24M × 9,200 = 57.408B ≈ 57.4B; 92,000 × 3,600 × 730 = 241.776B ≈ 241.8B; 87,600 / 57.408B = 1.526e-6 → 655K tokens/$1). The note correctly labels the 655K figure an hour-basis artifact. However, the note says the two figures 'differ only in the hour count in the denominator (173.33 vs 730), not in the workload or the fleet' — but the 655K figure divides a 730-hour spend by an active-hours (173.33 h) token volume, while the 2.76M figure divides a 173.33-hour spend by a 173.33-hour token volume. The phrase 'differ only in the hour count in the denominator' is imprecise: they also differ in the numerator's hour basis (730 h spend vs 173.33 h spend). The intended point — that the mismatch is an hour-basis artifact, not a workload or fleet difference — is correct, but the phrasing understates the numerator mismatch. Minor clarity issue.
fix_instruction: Rewrite as: 'the two figures differ only in which hour count is used for the spend (730 h paid vs 173.33 h active) while the token volume is always active-hours — an hour-basis mismatch, not a workload or fleet difference.'

issue: Malformed and colliding Appendix A cross-references. (a) The stated convention requires a letter suffix on section labels ('§ 9A'), but the body writes '§10', 'A.10', '§A.7' and '§9A' — four incompatible forms for section references. fix_instruction: Adopt one section form everywhere (e.g. 'Appendix A § 10A' style matching the stated 'letter suffix' rule) and convert every body instance ('Appendix A §10' p.3, 'A.10' p.74, '§A.7' p.100) to it; reserve bare 'A.N' for figures only, and rewrite the Preface's 'Appendix A, A.3' / 'A.6' / 'A.10' text-note references (PDF pp.17, 22) to the section form so they stop colliding with figure A.3 (PDF p.9).

evidence: Preface rule (PDF p.23): 'Do not repeat a chapter number after the chapter name — write Ch. 8 § 3 or § 8.3.3, not Ch. 8 § 8.3.3.' Violating instances: PDF p.48 'derived in Ch 4 §4.3 and carried in Table 4-2' and 'the ~64 GB runtime/workspace reserve that Ch 7 §7.1 states as an assumption'; PDF p.74 'Ch 7 §7.4 re-derives the per-token value for other geometries'; PDF p.125 'Chapter 14 §14.4 (Acceptance test for a quantized deployment)'; PDF p.142 'resident KV slots (Ch 4 §4.3, §4.6)'; PDF p.156 '6 hosts, Ch 4 §4.3)'. issue: Recurrence of a house-rule violation: six references repeat the chapter number after the chapter name, exactly the form the Preface forbids. Under the book's own parsing rule ('§ N.M means Chapter N, Section M' plus 'the section number may stand alone'), 'Ch 7 §7.4' resolves to Chapter 7, Section 7.4 (= §7.7.4), which does not exist, instead of the intended §7.4; the same mis-resolution applies to 'Ch 4 §4.3' (should be Ch 4 §3), 'Ch 7 §7.1' and 'Chapter 14 §14.4'.
fix_instruction: Sweep all six instances and drop the chapter digit from the section specifier: 'Ch 4 §4.3' → 'Ch 4 § 3' (PDF pp.48, 142, 156), 'Ch 7 §7.1' → 'Ch 7 § 1' (p.48), 'Ch 7 §7.4' → 'Ch 7 § 4' (p.74), 'Chapter 14 §14.4' → 'Chapter 14 § 4' (p.125); leave already-correct forms such as 'Ch 8 §3.4' (PDF p.32) unchanged.

fix_instruction: Replace '[ILLUSTRATIVE synthetic mixture]' (PDF p.121) with '[ILLUSTRATIVE][ASSUMPTION]' for inputs and '[ILLUSTRATIVE][DERIVED]' for the computed percentiles; replace '[ILLUSTRATIVE synthetic profile]' (Fig. 6.2, p.147) and '[ILLUSTRATIVE conceptual]' (Figs. 4.1, 5.1, 6.1 at pp.118, 141, 144, plus List of Figures pp.8–9) with the appropriate Axis-2 tag, moving any descriptive word outside the brackets.

evidence: Page 33 (§1.3): "If average request is ~9.2K input + ~300 output ≈ 9.5K tokens per request, and traffic is ~10 req/s, then the system ingests: • Input tokens/s: 9,200 tokens/req × 10 req/s = 92,000 tokens/s (peaks higher at ~40 req/s → ~368k). • Output tokens/s: 300 ×10 = 3,000 tokens/s output. • Roughly 30× more input tokens than output tokens in this workload (9,200 ÷ 300 ≈ 30.7, carried book-wide as the canonical ~30×, Ch. 4, Table 4-2)."

So the ratio's authoritative home (Table 1-1) contradicts the cross-reference Ch. 1 makes to Table 4-2.
fix_instruction: Either add an explicit input/output ratio row to Table 4-2 (Ch. 4, p. 76–79) with its [canonical scenario][DERIVED] status, or correct the Ch. 1 citations from "Ch. 4, Table 4-2" to "Table 1-1" so the ratio's provenance points at the table that actually records it.

evidence: Page 55 (Fig 3.4 caption): "1 expert = 5.7B params ≈ 11.4 GB (FP16)" and "MoE total resident ≈ 94 GB = 91 GB experts + 3 GB always-on"; the body text above the figure reads "per token: top-2 = 11.4B (2 × 5.7B) + 1.4B always-on = 12.8B → 25.6 GB".
issue: The figure's own arithmetic is internally inconsistent: 8 experts × 11.4 GB = 91.2 GB of experts plus the always-on block gives 91 + 3 = 94 GB resident, but the always-on block is stated elsewhere in the same chapter as ~1.4B params (≈2.8 GB at FP16), not 3 GB — and the figure's own body text uses 1.4B/25.6 GB for the active read (11.4 GB + 2.8 GB = 14.2 GB, not 25.6 GB). A reader cannot reconcile 2 × 5.7B (=11.4B) + 2.8 GB with a 25.6 GB read without silently recomputing 12.8B × 2 B = 25.6 GB, which is a different decomposition from the one printed.
fix_instruction: Fix the Fig 3.4 panel arithmetic so the always-on block is consistently ~1.4B params ≈ 2.8 GB (not 3 GB), and rewrite the per-token read line so it reads 'per token: 2 experts = 11.4B (2 × 5.7B) + 1.4B always-on = 12.8B active → 25.6 GB read (12.8B × 2 B)' rather than splitting 25.6 GB as '23 GB + 2.8 GB' while simultaneously printing 11.4B + 2.8 GB as the component sum.

fix_instruction: In the p. 96 sidebar table, add an explicit row-level pointer in the 6-host paid-occupancy row's Qualifier column naming the alternative hour-matched figure ($20,800/mo ≈ $3.33/1K) and mark the ≈$14.04 Per-1K cell as 'hour-basis mismatch, not comparable', so the two monthly figures for one fleet are reconciled inside the table rather than only in the p. 98 prose.

evidence: Page 37 (§1.5 Common Mistakes): "• Ignoring the input/output asymmetry. Treating a request as 'one unit' hides that input-heavy workloads tend toward high prefill compute and KV-capacity pressure, while output-heavy ones are decode-dominant (run-time per generated token) — opposite bottlenecks with opposite fixes. (Note: 'capacity pressure' is a memory-capacity constraint, not a memory-bandwidth bound; see Ch. 4/8.)"
issue: The cross-reference "see Ch. 4/8" is not a resolvable reference under the book's own convention. The Preface (p. xix) defines the reference form: "A section reference takes the form § N.M ... so § 7.3 and § 7.3 name the same reference" and "Do not repeat a chapter number after the chapter name — write Ch. 8 § 3 or § 8.3.3, not Ch. 8 § 8.3.3." "Ch. 4/8" names two chapters joined by a slash with no section anchor and no target topic — it does not resolve to a specific discussion, and Ch. 4's Chapter-Question scope (workload characterization) does not contain a capacity-vs-bandwidth distinction, while Ch. 8 (Compute) and Ch. 7 (Memory) do. The note's own content — that KV pressure is a capacity constraint rather than a bandwidth bound — is stated in Ch. 7 §7.3 (p. 143, the concurrency ceiling) and Ch. 8 (roofline), but Ch. 4 does not carry it as its defining content.
fix_instruction: Replace "see Ch. 4/8" with resolvable anchors that actually state the capacity-vs-bandwidth distinction, e.g. "see § 7.3 (concurrency ceiling) and § 8.2 (roofline ridge)", so the reference follows the book's § N.M convention and points at sections that discuss the cited point.

evidence: Page 132 (§6.8): "Hosts were raised from H = 1 to H = 21. That is the capacity floor, which is the max of the named screens, not the prefill compute screen alone: case (i)'s prefill screen needs ⌈18.6⌉ = 19 hosts, but the KV-residency / Little's-Law screen needs ⌈344/17⌉ = 21 hosts at the peak and therefore binds (Ch 8 §3; Ch 17)."
issue: The mini-case's own arithmetic contains a contradiction the text does not flag: it computes the fleet oversubscription as 51.6 ÷ (H × 2.77) = 18.6/H and then, two paragraphs earlier, says the 40 rps peak "demands 40 × 1.29 ≈ 51.6 PFLOP/s ≈ 18.6 host-equivalents" for a single host — but 51.6 ÷ 2.77 = 18.6, so 18.6 is the SINGLE-HOST requirement (H = 1), while the text then reads "the fleet oversubscription at peak is 51.6 ÷ (H × 2.77) = 18.6/H" and concludes "on the single host this mini-case assumes ... that is a ~4.7× oversubscription at baseline and 18.6× at the peak". The prefill screen for the fleet is then given as "⌈18.6⌉ = 19 hosts", i.e. the single-host-equivalent figure is used as the fleet host count without the reader being told that 18.6 is already a host-equivalent count (18.6 hosts needed), not an oversubscription ratio that must be divided by H again. The ratio and the absolute count are the same number used in two roles (an oversubscription factor at H=1 and a host count at fleet level), which is exactly the unit conflation the chapter elsewhere warns against.
fix_instruction: Rewrite the mini-case's prefill arithmetic to keep the two roles separate: state the peak prefill demand as 51.6 PFLOP/s, the single-host sustained capacity as 2.77 PFLOP/s, the host-equivalent requirement as 51.6 ÷ 2.77 ≈ 18.6 hosts, and the oversubscription at H hosts as 18.6/H — then take the prefill screen as ⌈18.6⌉ = 19 hosts explicitly as a host count (not a factor), and state that the KV-residency screen's 21 hosts is the binding one.

evidence: Page 33 (§1.3): "• Input tokens/s: 9,200 tokens/req × 10 req/s = 92,000 tokens/s (peaks higher at ~40 req/s → ~368k)." and "• Output tokens/s: 300 ×10 = 3,000 tokens/s output."
